facts.value: Bioinformatics relies heavily on data generated by various experimental techniques, which may vary in quality and accuracy.
Analyzing large datasets requires significant computational resources, leading to challenges in processing time and storage.
Existing algorithms may not always be able to accurately predict complex biological phenomena or interpret highly heterogeneous data.
Bioinformatics tools can provide correlations and patterns, but may not always elucidate the underlying biological mechanisms.
Integrating data from diverse sources, such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, can be challenging due to differences in data formats and experimental protocols.
Concerns related to privacy, data security, and ownership of biological data pose ethical and legal challenges in bioinformatics research and applications.
